messages:
Nora: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the Observability Insights PRD (retention + dashboard export UX) before next Wed. Fintech X asked for 1yr exports; infra flagged cost/regulatory tradeoffs. I put a proposed MVP below. Please respond with: approve / NACK + reason / follow-ups.

Proposed MVP (short):
- Retention tiers: default 30d, paid 90d, export-to-S3 for >=365d (on-demand).
- UI: simple dropdown on the dataset settings page + export modal.
- Backend: cold store to S3 for archived exports, periodic purge job, audit logs for deletions.
- Rollout: canary with opt-in orgs -> auto-enroll -> GA.

Acceptance criteria (what must be true to ship):
1) Storage and query cost estimates for 30/90/365d validated with infra and finance.
2) UX screens for set retention + export modal implemented and usability-checked.
3) Purge job and audit logging implemented; E2E export success rate >= 95% in canary.

Example retention config (for infra):
```yaml
retention:
  default_days: 30
  tiers:
    - name: standard
      days: 30
    - name: extended
      days: 90
    - name: archive
      days: 365
```

Emma: I like keeping the UI minimal — dropdown + a tiny tooltip that explains cost. Recommend free tier = 30d, paid = 90d, long-term via export. Also propose a canary flag so we can test query perf. :thumbsup:

Raj: Need infra numbers before final. Roughly: +12% storage cost for 90d vs 30d, +40% for 365d if stored hot. Query latency could regress for large orgs. Suggest we use cold store for >90d and a time-partitioned index for fast recent queries. Also +1 on canary.

Lina: UX note: default should be 30d. If user picks >90d show an explicit cost confirmation modal and a short explainer: "Longer retention increases storage costs and may affect query latency." Edge cases: what happens when a dataset is set to 365d and then downgraded — do we schedule immediate purge? Need decision.

Marco: Compliance points: deletion must be auditable. For GDPR/CCPA we need a hard-delete path and an audit record per deletion. If export-to-S3 is used, we need clear ownership and TTL controls on buckets. Also flag: retention purge should not accidentally delete data that is in active exports or snapshots.

Sam: Metrics to monitor from day 1: retention_bytes_by_org, retention_query_latency_90p, export_job_success_rate, purge_errors_count, audit_events_written. Also add an eval set to simulate canonical queries across retention ranges to measure perf regressions.

Nora: Proposed decision flow: ship MVP with 3-tier surface: 30d (free, default), 90d (paid add-on), export-to-S3 option for full-year archives. No soft-delete for MVP (hard delete after TTL) and audit logs required. Rollout: 1) opt-in canary (3 customers) 2) expand to beta orgs 3) GA.

Raj: +1 but require per-org storage caps and throttles on export jobs. Implementation note: batch purge job every 6h, with backoff on failures. Example cron: `0 */6 * * *`. We'll also add a compaction task for cold storage once/week.

Lina: I'll wireframe the dropdown + cost modal and the export flow (upload progress, retry). Also will design error states for export failures and for when purge is delayed. ETA Tue EOD for initial mocks.

Emma: If no major objections by EOD tomorrow I'll mark the PRD as ready for RFC and schedule a 30min RFC review next Wed.

deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/docs/rfcs/observability-insights-retention-1716347890 (draft). Reminder: add cost/estimates section.

Nora: Great — thanks everyone. Action items: Emma: formalize ship decision and timeline. Raj/Marco: finalize infra cost+compliance checklist. Lina: mockups. Sam: metrics dashboard + alert thresholds. I'll collate and update the PRD tomorrow morning.

Emma: sounds good.

Raj: one more ask — limit max retention selectable in UI per org by default to 365d, but allow enterprise override via contract.

Nora: noted. We'll add that as a non-functional requirement in PRD.

Emma: :white_check_mark:
